videos.title: How to use an AI assistant as an internal knowledge base for Postgres
videos.focus: Evaluating a source-linked internal knowledge assistant before trusting workplace answers
videos.summary: EDB’s five-minute demonstration follows a sales associate querying product specifications and compliance documents through an internal knowledge assistant. Timestamped chapters cover governed infrastructure, Slack delivery, document synchronization and assistant construction. The lesson is product-specific, so its useful evidence is the workflow and source-grounding checklist rather than unverified accuracy claims.
videos.why_it_matters: Use the demonstration to audit one internal assistant: define authoritative documents, test retrieval coverage, require source links beside answers, record unsupported responses and keep access controls plus refresh ownership explicit before wider employee use.

verification.content_review_basis: Reviewed EDB’s complete timestamped companion description and official Vimeo metadata binding the individual episode, EDB publisher identity and exact five-minute runtime; no audiovisual playback claim is made.

quality_review.learning_objective: Evaluate whether an internal knowledge assistant retrieves authoritative workplace evidence and exposes enough source context for accountable review.
quality_review.practical_action: Choose five known-answer document questions, record retrieved sources, flag unsupported responses and verify access plus refresh ownership before a wider pilot.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected after the protected YouTube and IBM players failed because this exact publisher video has a direct public full-episode player and detailed timestamped instruction.

content_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete timestamped EDB description covering the sales-associate scenario, governed Postgres infrastructure, Slack answers, document synchronization, assistant construction, source grounding and stated product limitations.

quality_review.promotional_assessment: EDB promotes Postgres AI Factory, but the document-authority, source-link, unsupported-answer and access-review checklist transfers to other internal assistants.
transferable_takeaways: Define authoritative documents and known-answer questions before measuring an assistant’s usefulness.
Require source links beside responses so reviewers can distinguish retrieval evidence from generated language.
Keep document refresh, access controls and unsupported-answer escalation owned by named people.

videos.title: Putting AI to work for integration
videos.focus: Deciding where generative AI assists integration while governance and guardrails remain explicit
videos.summary: IBM AI Academy’s Madhu Kochar explains how generative AI can assist integration work while governance, guardrails and resilient process design remain necessary. The publisher page identifies the instructor, a 5:31 runtime and three learning objectives. This is evergreen vendor-authored instruction, so organizations should test claims against their own integration workload.
videos.why_it_matters: Use the lesson to review one integration process: map systems and owners, identify the step AI may assist, define validation and rollback controls, and measure whether the change improves resilience or merely moves complexity into generated configurations.

verification.content_review_basis: Reviewed IBM’s complete companion lesson, named instructor, exact 5:31 runtime, three teaching objectives and public publisher player; no audiovisual playback claim is made.

quality_review.learning_objective: Translate a broad AI-integration proposal into a bounded process map with guardrails, validation, ownership and rollback evidence.
quality_review.practical_action: Select one integration step, name its source and destination systems, define validation checks, assign an owner and specify a rollback trigger.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected from six reviewed candidates because the short publisher lesson provides a distinct integration decision exercise and a second original video publisher.

content_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete IBM companion lesson on integration value, automation, governance, guardrails, resilience and the increasing role of agents, with named instructor and exact runtime.

quality_review.promotional_assessment: IBM promotes its integration portfolio, but the selected process-mapping and guardrail exercise is transferable without IBM products.
transferable_takeaways: Map the source, destination and accountable owner before adding generated integration logic.
Define validation and rollback controls for the exact step an assistant may change.
Measure resilience and correction effort instead of counting generated artifacts as value.

verification.content_review_basis: Read the complete publisher script, checked the exact October 26 episode route, 13:57 runtime and synthetic-voice disclosure; no audio playback claim is made.

quality_review.practical_action: For each item, record the primary URL, the decision it might change, one unsupported claim and whether deeper reading is warranted.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected for a complete current script, exact episode identity, transparent synthetic-voice disclosure and a show absent from the recent cooldown.

podcasts.title: Nearly 100 GEO Audits Later: What Big Brands Still Miss
podcasts.summary: The GEO Show’s hosts review patterns from nearly 100 generative-engine-optimization audits, including weak source authority, fragmented ownership and confusion between visibility and business outcomes. The exact episode page includes a full transcript and 46:20 runtime. The sample is consultancy-derived, so readers should treat patterns as hypotheses for local measurement.
podcasts.why_it_matters: Listeners get a practical audit sequence: define the business question, inspect which sources engines cite, separate mention frequency from conversion value, assign cross-functional ownership and rerun the same queries after changes instead of chasing a single visibility score.

verification.content_review_basis: Read the complete publisher transcript and checked the exact individual episode route, October 26 date and 46:20 runtime; no audio playback claim is made.

quality_review.learning_objective: Turn broad generative-search visibility claims into a repeatable audit that separates source presence, query coverage and business outcomes.
quality_review.practical_action: Select ten recurring customer questions, record cited sources and brand mentions, assign owners, make one bounded change and rerun the same query set.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected for its complete individual-episode transcript, concrete audit patterns, exact runtime and a distinct show absent from the recent cooldown.

content_evidence.scope: Read the complete transcript covering audit patterns, source authority, content structure, ownership gaps, visibility metrics, business outcomes and repeatable query testing.

quality_review.promotional_assessment: The reviewed transcript is primarily editorial analysis; any sponsorship or product references are not used as evidence for the selected takeaways.

editorial_segments.topic: Audit methodology, generative-engine visibility and initial source authority findings
Content structure, citation patterns and discoverability across recurring customer questions
Organizational ownership, measurement gaps and cross-functional implementation barriers
Business outcomes, repeated query tests and practical prioritization after an audit

quality_review.editorial_form_rationale: Human hosts synthesize patterns from their consultancy audits, distinguish operational observations from universal conclusions and propose a repeatable measurement process.
